newEntities.label: IL-13
newEntities.description: Th2 cytokine proposed as a candidate MCD mediator; experimental sufficiency in rats, human association only.

findings.quoteLocation: Europe PMC abstract; Results or Conclusions
findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: In a multicentre cohort, anti-nephrin autoantibodies were detected in 46 of 105 adults (44%) with MCD, rising to 69% in active MCD without immunosuppressive treatment.
findings.quote: In the subgroup of patients with active minimal change disease or idiopathic nephrotic syndrome who were not receiving immunosuppressive treatment, the prevalence of antinephrin autoantibodies was as high as 69% and 90%, respectively.
findings.studySystem: Multicentre cohort of 539 patients (357 adults, 182 children) and 117 controls; serum anti-nephrin assay
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Prevalence is cohort- and assay-dependent; the overall adult MCD figure (46/105, 44%) is lower than the active untreated subgroup.
Antibody-negative MCD is not explained by this finding.
findings.distinctFindingRationale: Cross-sectional prevalence is a separate result from the longitudinal disease-activity correlation in the same study.

findings.quoteLocation: Europe PMC abstract; Results or Conclusions
findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: Anti-nephrin autoantibody levels correlated with disease activity at inclusion and during follow-up.
findings.quote: At study inclusion and during follow-up, antinephrin autoantibody levels were correlated with disease activity.
findings.studySystem: Multicentre cohort of adults with MCD/FSGS and children with idiopathic nephrotic syndrome; serial antibody measurements
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Correlation with activity does not by itself establish pathogenicity in humans.
findings.distinctFindingRationale: Longitudinal correlation with disease activity is a separate result from the cross-sectional prevalence in the same study.

findings.quoteLocation: Europe PMC abstract; Results or Conclusions
findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: Active immunization of mice with recombinant nephrin induced nephrotic syndrome with an MCD-like phenotype, IgG at the slit diaphragm, nephrin phosphorylation and severe podocyte cytoskeletal changes.
findings.quote: Experimental immunization induced a nephrotic syndrome, a minimal change disease-like phenotype, IgG localization to the podocyte slit diaphragm, nephrin phosphorylation, and severe cytoskeletal changes in mice.
findings.studySystem: Mice actively immunized with recombinant murine nephrin
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Experimental sufficiency in mice; does not establish the mechanism or its prevalence in every human case.
Active immunization with murine nephrin differs from spontaneous human autoimmunity.

findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: Passive transfer of IgG from an anti-nephrin-positive MCD patient to a rabbit caused proteinuria and podocyte foot-process effacement without electron-dense deposits, absent in the control rabbit.
findings.quote: Further morphological workup revealed moderate podocyte foot process effacement in the absence of electron-dense deposits in the anti-nephrin rabbit by electron microscopy
findings.studySystem: New Zealand White rabbits given purified human IgG from plasma-exchange fluid of an anti-nephrin-positive MCD patient or control IgG; 5-day observation
limitations: IgG from a single patient was transferred to one rabbit, with one control rabbit; total IgG rather than purified nephrin-specific IgG was transferred.
Experimental induction in rabbits does not establish the mechanism in every human case or in antibody-negative disease.
Supplementary figures not inspected; independent domain review pending.

findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: Patient-derived anti-nephrin IgG bound glomerular nephrin and strongly increased nephrin tyrosine phosphorylation in the recipient rabbit.
findings.quote: Nephrin tyrosine phosphorylation strongly increased in response to human anti-nephrin autoantibodies
findings.studySystem: Rabbit passive-transfer model; glomerular nephrin immunoprecipitation and phosphorylation analysis
limitations: IgG from a single patient was transferred to one rabbit, with one control rabbit; total IgG rather than purified nephrin-specific IgG was transferred.
Experimental induction in rabbits does not establish the mechanism in every human case or in antibody-negative disease.
Supplementary figures not inspected; independent domain review pending.
The downstream sequence from phosphorylation to cytoskeletal change and effacement was not established.

findings.quoteLocation: Europe PMC abstract; Results or Conclusions
findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: In 596 biopsy-diagnosed adult Chinese patients with MCD or primary FSGS, anti-nephrin antibodies fell during clinical remission and reappeared before proteinuria relapse.
findings.quote: Longitudinal analysis revealed that anti-nephrin antibodies significantly decreased during clinical remission, while they reappeared preceding proteinuria relapse.
findings.studySystem: 596 adults (436 MCD, 160 primary FSGS); ELISA for anti-nephrin IgG and IgM with antigen-inhibition and Western blot validation
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Mixed MCD and primary FSGS cohort; MCD-specific longitudinal estimates are not separated in the abstract.
Different assay (ELISA, including IgM) from the multicentre immunoprecipitation-based cohort; prevalence is assay-dependent.

findings.quoteLocation: Europe PMC abstract; Results or Conclusions
findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: Anti-nephrin-positive MCD patients had a predominant IgG4 subclass with elevated serum IL-4 and IL-13 and an increased IL-4/IFN-gamma ratio, consistent with Th2 skewing.
findings.quote: anti-nephrin antibody-positive MCD patients displayed a predominant IgG4 subclass alongside elevated serum IL-4 and IL-13 levels and an increased IL-4/IFN-γ ratio, supporting a Th2-skewed immune status.
findings.studySystem: 60 patients with biopsy-confirmed MCD (including children), 125 other glomerular diseases, 40 controls; affinity capture-elution ELISA and Olink cytokine proteomics
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Cross-sectional association; does not show that Th2 cytokines drive antibody production or podocyte injury.
Small single-disease sample; links humoral and Th2 findings without establishing their sequence.

findings.quoteLocation: Europe PMC abstract; Results or Conclusions
findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: Anti-nephrin autoantibodies were detected in 50% of 60 MCD patients and 70% of those in active phase; levels correlated positively with proteinuria and inversely with serum albumin.
findings.quote: Anti-nephrin levels positively correlated with proteinuria, and inversely with serum albumin and estimated glomerular filtration rate.
findings.studySystem: 60 patients with biopsy-confirmed MCD across disease stages; affinity capture-elution ELISA
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Cross-sectional correlations; assay-dependent prevalence.

findings.quoteLocation: Europe PMC abstract; Results or Conclusions
findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: In 17 therapy-naive adults with biopsy-proven MCD, 12 were anti-nephrin positive; all 12 reached complete remission with undetectable antibodies after 8 weeks of steroids.
findings.quote: All 12 patients (100%) positive for anti-nephrin antibodies achieved complete remission with no anti-nephrin antibodies detectable after 8 weeks of steroid treatment (t 1 ).
findings.studySystem: Prospective sampling of 17 adults with newly diagnosed MCD at diagnosis and after 8 weeks of steroids; immunoprecipitation assay and B-cell flow cytometry
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Small uncontrolled cohort; antibody clearance and remission are concurrent and do not show that antibody reduction alone explains treatment benefit.
The authors’ statement that this explains the steroid response is not adopted as a causal claim.
findings.distinctFindingRationale: Antibody clearance with remission is a separate result from the plasmablast comparison already entered from this study.

findings.quoteLocation: Europe PMC abstract; Results or Conclusions
findings.subject: entity-il13
findings.text: IL-13 overexpression in rats produced albuminuria, hypoalbuminemia and up to 80% podocyte foot-process fusion without significant light-microscopic glomerular change.
findings.quote: electron microscopy showed up to 80% of podocyte foot process fusion
findings.studySystem: Wistar rats with IL-13 overexpressed by in vivo electroporation (n = 41) versus controls (n = 17)
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Experimental sufficiency of IL-13 overexpression in rats; does not establish that IL-13 is necessary or independently causal in human MCD.

findings.quoteLocation: Europe PMC abstract; Results or Conclusions
findings.subject: entity-il13
findings.text: IL-13 overexpression in rats downregulated glomerular nephrin, podocin and dystroglycan and upregulated B7-1 (CD80).
findings.quote: Glomerular gene expression was significantly upregulated for B7-1, IL-4Ralpha, and IL-13Ralpha2 but downregulated for nephrin, podocin, and dystroglycan.
findings.studySystem: Wistar rats with IL-13 overexpression; glomerular real-time PCR and immunofluorescence
limitations: Abstract-only agent inspection; independent domain review pending.
Experimental sufficiency of IL-13 overexpression in rats; does not establish that IL-13 is necessary or independently causal in human MCD.
Expression changes do not establish whether nephrin loss is upstream of effacement in this model.
